data.description:
## Context / Problem

The reducer stamps the claim-session provenance (`claimed_session`, `claim_harness`,
`claim_remote_session`) **only** on the winning `open -> in_progress` STATUS fold —
`_fold_claimed_session` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py:25`), keyed on
`current_status == "open" and status == "in_progress"`. Nothing ever clears it, so a
ticket that has left `in_progress` (closed / blocked / re-opened) still reports the last
claimer's session (documented behaviour, `docs/event-schema.md:250-255`). For the
cross-session warning (this ticket's parent) to mean "currently `in_progress` by session
X", the provenance must be **cleared on every exit from `in_progress`**.

A consumer scan confirms this is behaviour-safe: every reader of these three keys is pure
passthrough — the LLM compact-key map (`src/rebar/reducer/llm_format.py:44-46`
`csn`/`chn`/`rsn`), the MCP model fields (`src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:109-111`), the state
defaults (`src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:47-49`), the `TicketState` typing
(`src/rebar/types.py:123-125`), and the `txn.py` writer. Nothing branches on the value or
relies on it persisting past `in_progress`.

## Approach

In `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py`, add a sibling helper (e.g.
`_clear_claimed_session(state)`) that sets `state["claimed_session"]`,
`state["claim_harness"]`, and `state["claim_remote_session"]` to `None`, and invoke it on
a winning STATUS fold where `data["current_status"] == "in_progress"` and
`data["status"] != "in_progress"`. Invoke it in the **same two branches** where
`_fold_claimed_session` is applied — the normal-update branch
(`_processors_status.py:166`) and the fork-**winner** branch (`:139`) — and **never** in
the branch where the existing chain wins, so a losing concurrent transition cannot clear
the fork winner's provenance (mirrors the `_fold_claimed_session` fork-winner gating,
advisory G6/T8). The clear and the set are mutually exclusive per event (an event is
either entering or leaving `in_progress`), so ordering is irrelevant.

This is additive and forward/back-compatible: older clones ignore reducer-state shape;
`make_initial_state` already defaults these three keys to `None`
(`src/rebar/reducer/_state.py:47-49`), so a fresh replay and a snapshot-served state
agree, and a pre-feature SNAPSHOT that lacks a post-exit clear simply restores whatever it
stored (no migration of stored events — state is recomputed from the append-only log).
Rollback is trivial: reverting the reducer change restores the prior persist-past-exit
behaviour with no stored-data cleanup, because no event bytes change.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` — add the clear helper + invoke on the exit
  edge in the normal-update and fork-winner branches.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — document, in §"Session provenance (`claimed_session`)", that
  the three fields are cleared on every exit from `in_progress` (so a non-`in_progress`
  ticket reports no holder).

No new event type, no schema change (the keys already exist), no config.

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test against the real reducer** replaying real event sequences
(test-design §3 "pure calculation / validation branch" — the whole mechanism is the
reducer fold; no CLI/git/process boundary is crossed). Existing reducer tests live under
`tests/` next to the other `_processors`/reducer suites; inventory those first and extend
the nearest claim-session suite rather than duplicating fixtures.

- Happy path + collateral: replay `open -> in_progress` with `data["session"]="A"`,
  `data["harness"]="claude-code"`, `data["remote_session"]="R"`, then `in_progress ->
  closed`; assert the reduced state has all three of `claimed_session`, `claim_harness`,
  `claim_remote_session` equal to `None`.
- Parameterized exit edges: the same three-field clear holds for `in_progress -> blocked`,
  `in_progress -> open`, and `in_progress -> idea`.
- Negative control (behavior must NOT change): `open -> in_progress` with **no** later
  exit leaves `claimed_session == "A"` (and the two siblings set) — proves the change
  only clears on exit, not on entry.
- Fork gating: given a STATUS fork on the exit edge, a **losing** concurrent
  `in_progress -> closed` event does not clear the fork-**winner**'s `claimed_session`
  (the winner keeps its holder); assert against the lexical-UUID winner already used by
  `_fold_claimed_session`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replaying `open->in_progress(session=A,harness=claude-code,remote_session=R)` then
  `in_progress->closed` yields reduced state with `claimed_session`, `claim_harness`,
  `claim_remote_session` all `None` (checked by a new reducer test, e.g.
  `test_claim_session_cleared_on_close`, run under `make test`).
- [ ] The same clearing holds for `in_progress->blocked`, `in_progress->open`, and
  `in_progress->idea` (checked by a parameterized reducer test over those exit statuses).
- [ ] Negative control: `open->in_progress` with no subsequent exit leaves
  `claimed_session=="A"` (checked by a reducer test asserting the field persists while
  `in_progress`).
- [ ] A losing concurrent exit STATUS in a fork does not clear the fork-winner's
  `claimed_session` (checked by a reducer fork test asserting the winner's holder is
  intact).
- [ ] `docs/event-schema.md` §"Session provenance" states the three fields are cleared on
  every exit from `in_progress` (checked: `grep -n "cleared on" docs/event-schema.md`
  matches the new sentence).
data.title: Clear claim-session provenance on every exit from in_progress (reducer)
